reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes participation in the OneCoin system by showing viewers how to place buy and sell orders, purchase tokens, and submit those tokens to a mining process that is presented as producing coins and profit. The speaker describes personal token purchases and mining balances, then directs viewers through the exchange and mining workflow, making this an active solicitation rather than neutral market commentary.

citations.quote: Okay, so let me go in and show you how to do mining.
those tokens went into a mining operation at 12 tokens per Coin
another $180,000 come into my account, and those have been submitted for mining
if you want to buy and sell the coins
profit through our

opening.argument: The speaker presents a limited, conditional walkthrough rather than a promise of returns. He describes a “simple example,” acknowledges that an order cannot proceed because of the minimum, and explains that the demonstration depends on the viewer’s own account and available tokens. Nothing in these statements guarantees profit, appreciation, or successful mining; they describe what the interface permits the speaker to attempt. The cautious operational framing matters because showing a process is not the same as certifying its financial outcome.

citations.quote: I'll just make a simple example I want to buy one coin
A minimum order of ten coins, so I can't do anything right now in this particular account.
if I had I extra tokens which I do not right now

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats the existence of mining and trading instructions as proof of deceptive solicitation, but those instructions do not establish a guaranteed return. The cited description says users can “profit,” yet it does not state that profit is assured, and the video itself describes account-specific conditions and limitations. A conditional demonstration should not be converted into a promise the speaker never makes.

citations.quote: profit through our
A minimum order of ten coins, so I can't do anything right now in this particular account.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of an explicit guarantee does not remove the promotional implication. The speaker does more than warn viewers about uncertainty: he explains how to buy coins, submit tokens into mining, and track the resulting coin production. His personal account examples make the process appear operational and beneficial, while the description expressly connects the system with profit.

citations.quote: that is how you would buy coins
those tokens went into a mining operation at 12 tokens per Coin
profit through our

opening.argument: The strongest reading is an operational tutorial. The title explicitly identifies the subject as how to buy and sell OneCoins and tokens, and the narration repeatedly explains where to click, what fields to complete, and how to inspect account information. The speaker does not make a personal appeal for money or describe a recruitment opportunity; he demonstrates navigation through an exchange and account dashboard. Even the mining discussion is presented as an explanation of how the platform records token allocations and rates, not as independent proof that viewers will earn money.

citations.quote: How to Buy/Sell OneCoins/Tokens 2015
You would come on Ask and you would come in to ask and you can go in and sell the coins
This allows you to keep track of all the coins all the tokens that you have going into mining

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the video a tutorial does not answer what the tutorial teaches. It guides viewers through purchasing, selling, and assigning tokens to mining, then closes by directing them back to the exchange. That is actionable participation guidance, not detached software instruction. The speaker’s first-person account examples further present the system as something to use, rather than merely analyze.

citations.quote: if you want to buy and sell the coins
that is how you trade internally within our platform
those tokens went into a mining operation at 12 tokens per Coin

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The procedural format is precisely what makes the promotion actionable. The video does not merely explain generic exchange concepts; it demonstrates this platform’s buy and sell controls and links token balances to coin generation. A tutorial can still solicit participation when its practical lesson is how to enter the system and use its earning mechanism.

citations.quote: Okay, so let me go in and show you how to do mining.
So that is how you buy coins and sell coins.
that's how I got the 10,000 coins on this account

opening.argument: The demonstrated activity resembles ordinary platform commerce: users place market orders, see a stated price, pay a transaction fee, and receive the transaction in an account. The interface shows buying and selling rather than a downline, recruitment structure, or guaranteed payout. The narration also identifies concrete trading conditions, including a minimum order and a fee. Those details are consistent with an internal exchange service; the supplied evidence does not establish that the service was safe, but lack of proof of safety is not proof of a scam mechanism.

citations.quote: A minimum order of ten coins
25 cent transaction fee
you're getting a dollar 45 if you want to buy them you're getting a dollar 55

rebuttal.rebuttal: The ordinary-commerce label overlooks the central mechanism being demonstrated: purchased tokens are submitted to mining and described as producing coins. The speaker also associates substantial account amounts with that process. A transaction fee and visible prices do not neutralize a system whose central appeal is coin generation from token participation.

citations.quote: those tokens went into a mining operation at 12 tokens per Coin
another $180,000 come into my account, and those have been submitted for mining

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The exchange features are not the whole message. The speaker expressly says tokens are put into mining at changing rates and uses his account to explain how those actions produced coins. That connects ordinary-looking orders to a paid mining-return mechanism; the absence of a downline does not resolve that concern.
